scenarios.name: decode_yparity_0_1
scenarios.description: Sender signature v byte as 0/1 instead of 27/28. The node accepts it.

skipReasons.go: tempo-go Deserialize accepts a 0/1 sender v byte and re-encodes it as 27/28 (pkg/transaction/serialize.go:346), so Tx.Hash() of the decoded transaction is the hash the node reports for it, not keccak256 of the bytes received that this vector expects. tempo-go <= v0.6.1 hashed the received 0/1 encoding, which this vector expects; tempo-go#135 switched to the node behaviour, so from the next release on it reports the node's hash.
skipReasons.python: pytempo has no API to decode a signed transaction or recover its sender or fee payer (pytempo/models.py: encode() and from_dict() only). Fixed by pytempo#134 (https://github.com/tempoxyz/pytempo/pull/134), merged but not yet released (release PR pytempo#135, 0.7.0).
skipReasons.rust: tempo-primitives AASigned decode hashes the 27/28 re-encoding, not the received bytes (crates/primitives/src/transaction/tt_signed.rs:96-104, :268). Same code as the node: see the node knownIssue on this case. Not fixed: the node itself reports this hash.

knownIssue.reason: The node accepts v = 0/1 but re-encodes it as 27/28 and reports the hash of that re-encoding, so keccak256 of the bytes the client sent (what every SDK returns as the hash) is a hash the node never knows.
